tadashi-yanai.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
tadashi-yanai.summary: Yanai publicly advocates economic-policy changes. Having a prominent platform does not establish that officials delivered his preferred policies or a preferential business benefit.
tadashi-yanai.mechanism: Public economic-policy advocacy; outcomes and reciprocal benefit unresolved

support.text: In a TIME interview, Yanai urged higher interest rates, fewer handouts and regulatory reform, while criticizing Japan’s political leadership.

counter.text: The same profile describes the retail expansion of his father’s small business. Neither business success nor outspoken criticism establishes a state-granted advantage.

tadashi-yanai.limitations: No numerical estimate: policy advocacy is observable, but implemented influence and reciprocal economic benefit are not established here. This is not a full review of Fast Retailing’s government relations or international supply chain.

iris-fontbona.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
iris-fontbona.period: Chilean business-group research covering 2010–2020, published 2023; ownership profile, January 2024
iris-fontbona.summary: Research documents political resources around the Luksic business group. Fontbona’s ownership role matters, but group-level evidence does not yet isolate her personal direction of political activity or a reciprocal benefit.
iris-fontbona.mechanism: Controlling family wealth, revolving-door networks and media interests; individual attribution unresolved

support.text: El País describes Fontbona’s control of foundation boards above the family holdings, while her sons lead business divisions. She is not simply an unrelated passive observer.

A peer-reviewed study identifies former public officials on Luksic-group boards, campaign financing and media interests as political resources. These observations concern the group and named family members, not automatically Fontbona’s personal decisions.
support.source: Atenea: Oligarquía, poder material y recursos de poder en Chile, 2010–2020

counter.text: El País distinguishes ownership-level influence from operating roles and says Fontbona does not sit on the listed companies’ boards. That distinction limits personal attribution; it does not remove ownership power.
The study distinguishes the Luksic group’s earlier commercial origins from its later participation in privatizations. It does not describe every part of the fortune as originating in privatization.

iris-fontbona.limitations: No numerical estimate until the individual-versus-family unit of assessment is resolved with more evidence. The Forbes “& family” label is a wealth attribution, not permission to assign every relative’s political conduct to the named person. Group-level scholarly classification is retained, not presented as an individual criminal finding.

zhong-shanshan.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
zhong-shanshan.period: Wuyishan agreement, 2017; park controversy, 2020; public backlash, March 2024
zhong-shanshan.summary: Nongfu Spring’s water project involved local-government cooperation and environmental controversy. That warrants scrutiny of allocation and oversight, but the reviewed material does not establish Zhong personally receiving political favors.
zhong-shanshan.mechanism: Local-government investment agreement and water access; preferential terms unresolved

support.text: ThinkChina reports an August 2017 investment agreement with Wuyishan’s local government, designated a key provincial project. The report does not establish whether the terms were preferential.
support.access: Indexed article passages reviewed; direct page retrieval failed

counter.text: The same account reports park authorities placing the disputed water-intake location outside the park boundary. The original allegation alone cannot establish unlawful construction inside the park.
counter.access: Indexed article passages reviewed; direct page retrieval failed

counter.text: CNA describes nationalist online attacks and Zhong’s denial of claims about his rivalry with Wahaha’s founder. These are not a government finding of corruption or proof of political control.

zhong-shanshan.limitations: No score: company-government cooperation is not itself a preferential exchange, and social-media hostility is not proof for or against oligarchy. The underlying project agreement and individual decision-making still require review; no nationality-based inference is made.

alexey-mordashov.reviewDepth: Source-led review of stated episodes; broader coverage still limited
alexey-mordashov.period: EU designation, February 2022; General Court judgment, September 2023
alexey-mordashov.summary: The EU attributed political-benefit and regime-support links to Mordashov’s holdings, and his 2023 sanctions challenge failed. Those records are substantial evidence to examine, but different legal grounds must not be collapsed into a proven personal patronage bargain.
alexey-mordashov.mechanism: Banking, media and industrial holdings ↔ attributed state support and benefit

support.text: The 2022 EU statement attributes benefit from political links and describes Severgroup’s connections to Bank Rossiya, National Media Group and Power Machines. These are the Council’s stated reasons, not a criminal conviction.

The General Court dismissed Mordashov’s challenge. Its summary includes the criterion covering leading businesspeople in revenue-generating sectors; that criterion is not itself a finding of a personal favor.

counter.text: Paragraph 118 records a contractual clause intended to prevent the turbines’ installation in Crimea, while explaining why it did not defeat the material-support ground. This preserves the defense without misreporting it as a successful challenge.

alexey-mordashov.limitations: No numerical estimate from this legal-record review alone. The underlying benefit mechanism and person-level political leverage need independent corroboration. This file describes historical reasons and a specific judgment, not an assertion about all current holdings, current sanctions in every jurisdiction, or criminal guilt.
